key_insight: Differentiable inverse rendering recovers per-pixel optical attenuation from a single OCT image by optimizing a physics-based model without training data or segmentations.
clinical_relevance: Quantitative attenuation maps could support tissue characterization in intravascular OCT, but clinical diagnostic benefit remains unestablished.
method: Model OCT image formation with a differentiable physics-based forward model.
Use gradient descent to estimate per-pixel attenuation from one image.
Keep the optimization procedure unchanged when replacing the forward model or target optical parameter.
evidence_signal: The method was verified against analytical solutions, validated on five in vitro phantoms, and applied without modification to 29,269 clinical intravascular OCT images from 128 patients.
watch_item: Application to clinical images does not establish diagnostic accuracy; model assumptions and cross-platform robustness need further evaluation.
paper_title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography
